# Stress tests: where carrying should appear {#sec-stress}

The principle could be an artifact of the settings in which we found it. When every
layer can read every earlier position, carrying is never necessary. When the
content is visible in the text, it can always be re-read. We therefore test three
settings chosen to break it: an architecture in which most layers can pass
information forward only by carrying it, a distance at which most attention layers
cannot reach the source, and content that is not in the text at all. Each test had a
decision rule fixed before its first result (Appendix @sec-app-prereg).
@fig-stress summarizes the three.

![Stress tests. **A:** Qwen3.5 hybrids, in which three of every four layers are

1,024-token window of its local layers (shaded), direct retrieval of the rhyme word
falls. The copy at the line's final token becomes necessary for about half of

## Recurrent memory {#sec-recurrent}

Qwen3.5 [@qwen2026qwen35] interleaves three Gated DeltaNet layers
[@yang2025gateddeltanet] with each full-attention layer. A recurrent layer holds a
fixed-size state that is updated position by position. In those layers, information
from the source can reach a later position only by being carried in that state. This
is relay by construction, and invisible in the text. We split persistence by layer
type. In the *attention-only* cell, the donor state enters at the source, but the
input of every recurrent layer at the source is restored to its clean value, so the
edit can move forward only through the full-attention layers. The *recurrent-only*
cell is the converse. A cell with both routes blocked is a sanity check. The rule
fixed in advance was "go" if recurrent-only is at least 25% of persistence with its
interval above zero, and "stop" if it is below 10%. The decision is made on the
largest model; smaller sizes give the scale trend.

The recurrent memory does not carry the plan. At 4B and 9B (40 couplets each), the
recurrent-only cell is \(+0.28\) [0.07, 0.49] and \(+0.55\) [0.31, 0.79]: 3% and 4% of
persistence. The attention-only cell accounts for 97% and 96%. At the decisive size, 27B
(48 recurrent and 16 attention layers; 24 couplets), recurrent-only is \(+0.41\)
[0.18, 0.64], 2% of persistence \(+18.8\) [16.3, 21.3], and attention-only 95%. The
both-blocked cell is exactly zero in every model. Decision: stop. Even when three
quarters of the network can pass the plan forward only by carrying it, the plan
travels by direct retrieval through the quarter that can look it up.
\pending{Qwen3.5-27B at 100 couplets; Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (mixture of experts).}

## Beyond the attention window {#sec-distance}

Gemma 3 alternates five local layers with a 1,024-token sliding window with one
global layer [@gemma3; @beltagy2020longformer]. Once line 1 lies more than 1,024
tokens before the rhyme position, five of six layers can no longer read it. We
insert \(D\) tokens of neutral filler, a seeded arrangement of fixed everyday
sentences, at the start of the model's turn, followed by a fixed cue (`Next line:`).
The model then writes line 2. Relay is split into three groups: the boundary (the
prompt positions after line 1), the filler, and the generated text (the cue and
line 2). The frozen decision number is the share of persistence relayed through the
generated text: "go" at 25% or more, "stop" below 10%, and extension to 50 couplets
in between. A full-attention control, Qwen3-14B, showed before the Gemma result
that relay *shares* can rise with distance only because direct retrieval weakens.
We therefore added, before that result, the rule that a rise counts only if
absolute relay also grows.

@tbl-distance gives the extended run. At 2,000 tokens, Gemma 3 27B still writes a
rhyming line 2 in 82% of couplets. It reads less of the plan from the rhyme word:
direct retrieval falls from 66% to 40% of persistence. It relies instead on the copy
at the line's final token. That copy is necessary for \(+13.0\) [10.0, 16.1] of a
persistence of \(+26.4\), about half. Absolute relay grows about thirteenfold, and
mostly through the boundary. Relay along the generated text rises from about 1% to
12% by sufficiency (\(+3.2\) [2.2, 4.3]), and its necessity is \(+2.7\) (10%). The filler relays nothing (\(+0.3\) and \(+0.15\)). By the frozen rule, 12% falls between
"stop" and "go". It is the largest generated-text relay we observe in any setting,
and it remains about an eighth of the effect.

::: {#tbl-distance}

```{=latex}

\midrule
line 2 rhymes with line 1 & 98\% & 82\%\\
persistence & $+42.4$ [38.6, 46.0] & $+26.4$ [23.8, 28.9]\\
direct retrieval & $+28.0$ (66\%) & $+10.5$ (40\%)\\
line-end copy: sufficiency / necessity & $+0.1$ / $+4.6$ (11\%) & $+9.7$ / \textbf{$+13.0$} (49\%)\\
filler: sufficiency / necessity & 0.0 / 0.0 & $+0.3$ / $+0.2$\\
```

Relay at a distance, Gemma 3 27B (chat prompt; 50 couplets per distance; 95%
intervals). Shares are of persistence at the same distance.

:::

Two models without a strong line-end copy show what happens when lookup fails.
Gemma 3 12B (24 couplets), which stores little at the line end (@tbl-storage), loses
the plan at 2,000 tokens. Its line 2 is still a poem line, but it never rhymes with
line 1 (0 of 23), and persistence is \(+0.6\) [\(-0.7\), 1.8]. In the Qwen3.5-9B
hybrid, whose full-attention layers have no window, rhyming falls from 92% to 4%.
What remains of persistence (\(+3.6\)) is still 81% direct retrieval, and absolute
relay does not grow (\(+1.2\) to \(+0.8\)). The full-attention control, Qwen3-14B,
largely abandons the task after the filler (8% rhyming), and its absolute relay stays
flat (\(+2.3\) to \(+2.8\)). Across the four models, distance moves reliance onto a
stored copy where one exists, and otherwise costs the plan. No model responds by
carrying the plan along the text it writes. The rhyme word and the line's final token
lie at the same distance from the target. The global layers nevertheless read the
line-end token, which fits the view of separator tokens as long-range summaries of
their segment [@chen2024sepllm; @wang2023labelwords; @xiao2024sinks].
\pending{window curve at \(D=500, 1{,}000, 1{,}500\), predicted to change between
1,000 and 1,500 tokens.}

## Hidden content {#sec-hidden}

In every task so far, the content is visible: a reader of the text could recover the
rhyme sound from line 1, or the value from the operands. The case monitoring cares
about is content that cannot be recovered from the text. We create it with a secret
choice. The prompt reads: "Secretly choose one fruit from this list: {4 fruits}. Do not
write your choice yet. First write one sentence about the weather. Then write the
fruit you chose." Under greedy decoding the pick is a deterministic function of the
prompt. It depends on the model's own preferences and on the list order, so no
reader can compute it. For the route split, the model's turn is prefilled with a
fixed weather sentence and "The fruit I chose is". The outcome is the log-odds of the
donor's pick against the original pick at the next token.

**Mostly re-derived, partly stored, barely relayed.** The donor is the same list in
another order, chosen so that the greedy pick differs. The reference is a *text
swap*: the donor order written into the prompt, which moves the pick by
construction. In Qwen3-8B, Gemma 3 12B and Gemma 3 27B (100 pairs each), donor states
at the prompt positions after the list move the reveal by 12%, 15% and 16% of the
text swap. The reveal reads all of it directly: the retrieval cell equals the
post-list effect. Relay through the sentence is \(+0.00\) [\(-0.04\), 0.05],
\(-0.06\) [\(-0.14\), 0.01] and \(-0.01\) [\(-0.10\), 0.08]. It is also zero within
its interval in Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-14B. The one exception is Qwen3-32B, where the
post-list block holds 16% of the text swap. There, relay through the sentence is small
but nonzero: \(+0.06\) [0.04, 0.09], one eighth of the stored part and 2% of the text
swap. The recurrent hybrid Qwen3.5-27B behaves similarly. There, relay of the stored
part through the sentence is \(+0.03\) [0.02, 0.04], or 1% of the text swap. The sentence positions themselves account for 7% of the text swap (\(+0.15\) [0.12, 0.18]), the largest share
in any model; Qwen3-4B has 5% and every other model at most 1%. This is expected when every
position's recurrent state summarizes the prefix, including the list. The rest of the pick
is re-derived at the reveal from the visible list.

**The stored part is the choice itself.** An order swap cannot separate a stored
pick from a stored copy of the list order. In the out-of-list control, the donor
list shares no item with the original, so the donor's pick does not occur in the
prompt at all. The frozen criterion is that post-list donor states raise the absent
pick. It holds in every model. After the first results we identified a confound:
the positions might hold a copy of the donor's list rather than its pick. We
therefore added, post hoc, *pick specificity*: the effect on the donor's pick minus
the mean effect on the donor's other items. We then pre-registered it as the primary
measure of a replication in a second domain (animals; disjoint lists of six).

A same-pick null, frozen before its result, gives the converse check. The donor is the
same list in another order with the *same* pick. Post-list donor states then leave the
relative preference for the pick unchanged on average in Gemma 3 12B: \(-0.19\)
[\(-0.53\), 0.16], against a pick specificity of \(+1.01\) [0.78, 1.24] with out-of-list
donors. Individual pairs still move in both directions, because the block also holds order information about the rest of the list.

The replication confirms a stored, pick-specific choice in both families
(@fig-stress C; @tbl-hidden). The two families diverge with scale. In Gemma 3 the
stored share is largest at 27B in both domains (40% and 31%). The pre-registered
monotone prediction (4B below 12B below 27B) is only partly supported, because 4B
stores more than 12B. In Qwen3 the stored share shrinks with scale, from 10 to 15% at
8B to 0 to 7% at 14B and 32B. Qwen3.5-27B stores 3 to 4%. Larger Qwen models re-derive
the pick at the reveal.

::: {#tbl-hidden}

```{=latex}
\footnotesize
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3.5pt}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccccccc@{}}
\toprule
 & Qwen3-8B & Qwen3-14B & Qwen3-32B & Qwen3.5-27B & Gemma 3 4B & Gemma 3 12B & Gemma 3 27B\\
\midrule
Fruits & 10\% & 0\% & 2\% & 3\% & 18\% & 15\% & 31\%\\
Animals (pre-registered) & 15\% & 3\% & 7\% & 4\% & 22\% & 18\% & 40\%\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
```

Stored hidden pick: pick specificity of the post-list edit as a share of the
text-swap pick specificity (100 pairs per cell; values with 95% intervals in Appendix
@sec-app-hidden). Fruits: specificity added post hoc. Animals: pre-registered.

:::

**Not written into the text either.** In the free version, the model writes its own
weather sentence. The sentence changes with the donor in 17 to 45% of pairs, but it
never names an item. Emission is \(+0.02\) [\(-0.03\), 0.08], \(-0.01\) [\(-0.07\), 0.04]
and \(-0.00\) in Qwen3-8B, Gemma 3 12B and Gemma 3 27B. The sentence is not a covert
channel for the pick.

**Where the choice is stored.** Per-token necessity over the post-list block localizes
the stored pick (@fig-sites B). In Gemma 3 27B, 77% of the pick-specific effect
(\(+1.91\) [1.57, 2.24] of \(+2.48\)) sits on a single token: *the* in "about the
weather". The period after the list accounts for \(+0.42\), and the period ending the
instruction \(+0.22\). Every other token, including the end-of-turn and role tokens,
is \(0.00\pm0.05\). Gemma 3 12B uses the same site, both with fruits (*the*: \(+0.52\) of
\(+1.03\); the period after the list: \(+0.32\)) and with animals (*the*: \(+1.04\)
[0.80, 1.28] of \(+1.42\), or 73%). The site therefore replicates across two sizes
and two domains with the same wording. Gemma 3 4B stores as much of the pick (18%)
but places it differently: on the period that closes the instruction (\(+0.78\)
[0.65, 0.91], 58%) and the period that closes the list (\(+0.44\), 33%), with only
7% on *the*. The decisive check, frozen before its result, changes the wording. If the
storage moves with the function words, it is register-like storage at a predictable
token. If it stays at a fixed position or spreads out, the site is template-specific.
With the instruction reworded to "Keep your choice private for now. Begin by
describing today's weather in a single sentence. After that, reveal which fruit you
picked.", Gemma 3 12B stores 12% of the text swap's pick specificity (\(+0.59\) [0.38,
0.81]). The storage again concentrates on two low-content tokens. The period that ends the list accounts for \(+0.42\) [0.21, 0.63] (71%). The apostrophe of "today's", the token before "weather", accounts for \(+0.16\) [0.09, 0.22] (27%). Every other token is below 0.04.
The function-word site moved with the wording, which supports storage at a predictable
low-content token. Across sizes and wordings the stored pick concentrates on two or
three low-content tokens. These are the punctuation that closes a segment (the list,
or the instruction) and, from 12B on, a function word of the instruction that moves
with the wording. Segment-closing punctuation is the analogue of the line's final
token for rhymes: in both tasks the model stores a copy once, at a boundary next to
the source or at a predictable token of the prompt, and reads it at the point of
use. \pending{reworded instruction and animals at Gemma 3 27B; same-pick
null at Gemma 3 27B and Qwen3-32B.}
